EVIDENCE_CORRECTION_2026-09-17.root_cause_of_identical_frames: BY DESIGN, not a defect. Reproduced directly: manually wrote resolved content to app.py without `git add` and confirmed `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` (exactly what WorktreeView's getConflictedFiles() runs) STILL lists app.py as conflicted -- git's 'conflicted' state is an INDEX property (unresolved stage 1/2/3 entries), not a working-tree-content property. resolveConflictsWithAI() deliberately never `git add`s the resolved file (the human-review-before-commit safety contract), so the conflict banner and the DIFF panel's underlying `conflicted` array never change after a successful resolve. Separately, the DIFF panel itself renders `git diff HEAD` INSIDE THE SELECTED WORKTREE'S OWN DIRECTORY (feature-conflict/), which is a different filesystem location from where the conflict actually lives (the main repo) -- so it was always going to read clean, unrelated to the conflict resolution.
